production.note: US model years. First: Subaru of America's release 'Subaru Announces 2004 Impreza WRX STi Pricing; The Most Powerful Subaru Ever Offered for Sale in North America'. Last: Subaru's 2008 release introduces the all-new 'third-generation' 5-door WRX STI and compares it with "the 2007 WRX STI sedan" (subaru-us-2008-sti-release).

body.note: 'Review: 2004 Subaru WRX STi Sedan'. The 2008 Subaru release also calls the 2007 car 'the 2007 WRX STI sedan' (subaru-us-2008-sti-release).

displacementL.note: Subaru gives litres only ('2.5 liter'); no opened page gives a cc figure. Carey Russ's spec panel gives '2.5 liters / 150 cu. in.' (tac-2004-sti-russ).

aspiration.note: 'Intercooled and turbocharged DOHC boxer engine' (single turbocharger)

fuel.note: Inferred from the release's description of the turbocharged petrol boxer engine.

drivetrain.note: 'Full-Time All-Wheel Drive system with a Driver Control Center Differential (DCCD)'

powerHp.note: 2004 launch rating. Quote: "delivering 300 horsepower at 6000 RPM and 300 lb-ft. peak torque at 4000 RPM". The car was re-rated lower later in the run: Subaru's 2008 release gives the new car "305-horsepower...a gain of 12 over the previous model" (subaru-us-2008-sti-release), implying 293 hp for the 2007 car. The lower rating did not cover more than half of the model years, so the launch figure is used.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: two smaller publications, one without a named author. 2004 WRX STi sedan, 6-speed manual (the only car). Quote: "3263 lbs." (curb weight line of the specification panel in Carey Russ's review on The Auto Channel). MotorWeek's 2004 comparison test, with no author named, agrees: the two cars have "identical 3,263-pound curb weights" (motorweek-2004-sti-vs-evo, a publication). Subaru's releases give no curb weight.

provisionalNote: Weight is provisional: 3,263 lb rests on Carey Russ's spec panel on The Auto Channel and on MotorWeek's comparison test (no named author); the two agree, but neither is a major magazine and only one has a named author. A Subaru of America specification sheet, or a Car and Driver, Road & Track or MotorTrend spec panel for a 2004 STi, would replace it.
